_comment: Social-platform registry and its base-rate controls, for WebPivot/tools/wp_extract.py::extract_socials / extract_telegram. A social handle is operator-controlled contact infra, so a reused one clusters an operator's properties — which is exactly why the boilerplate here must be excluded: a site-builder's OWN accounts and a platform's utility paths are carried by every tenant. RULE 1: generic platform constants only, never a case handle.

social_hosts._comment: Host -> network name. A link to one of these hosts is read as a social account for that network. Matched exact or as a parent domain, so `m.facebook.com` resolves via `facebook.com`. Add a platform here to start recognising it; the value is the network label used in the `social:<network>:<handle>` indicator id.

boilerplate_social_handles._comment: `host/path` pairs that are the SITE BUILDER's own accounts, injected into every tenant's footer. Clustering on one links every Wix/Shopify/Squarespace/Webflow site ever built. Matched exactly against the lowercased `host/path` with any trailing slash removed.

telegram_boilerplate._comment: First path segments on t.me that are Telegram's OWN utility endpoints, not a channel or user: share widgets, the instant-view renderer, the URL shortener. A link to t.me/share is a share button on the page, not the operator's channel.
